text:
emma_cs: Hey team, new onboarding for 'PineApps' is spiking with 429s and a few `insufficient_quota` auth errors during Node SDK warmup. They reported ~230 concurrent session opens. Can infra advise quick fixes?

customer-dev: Logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-09-10T12:05:02Z] sess=ua-01 auth=ok token_age=2s status=200 req=aa11
[2026-09-10T12:05:02Z] sess=ua-02 auth=failed error=insufficient_quota
[2026-09-10T12:05:02Z] sess=ua-03 status=429 message="rate limit exceeded"
```
Init snippet they used:
```
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.preflight(); // called on every tab/session open
```

raj_eng: This looks like the classic preflight fanout / token stampede. Quick, high-impact mitigations you can ask the customer to apply right now:
- stop calling preflight on every tab/session open; do it once per process or once per session
- cache the preflight result for ~30-60s per process
- add randomized splay/jitter before any preflight during warmup (50-350ms)
- use one session-scoped ephemeral token rather than a token-per-request pattern
- enable http2 keepalives / connection reuse to reduce TCP churn

emma_cs: Can you paste a minimal copy-paste snippet we can send them? Keep it tiny.

raj_eng: Sure, drop this: 
```
// process-level cached preflight + jitter (Node)
let _pf = {ts:0,res:null};
async function getPreflight(client){
  if (Date.now()-_pf.ts < 45000) return _pf.res; // 45s cache
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, Math.floor(Math.random()*300)+50));
  _pf = {ts: Date.now(), res: await client.preflight()};
  return _pf.res;
}
```

logs-bot: Alert: key=rw_live_zx12 triggered onboarding-throttle at 2026-09-10T12:05:02Z. Window=120s peak_rps=63 avg_rps=16. Suggest lowering concurrent preflight to <=20 or request a short warmup bump.

customer-dev: Implemented the snippet (45s cache + splay) and dropped warmup concurrency to 18. Quick canary shows 429s went from ~34% sessions to ~2.5%.

emma_cs: Great! Two ops follow-ups: (1) I'll open a short support ticket if they need a temporary bump above 20 for a short warmup window; (2) please capture canary timestamps and token_age in logs so we can correlate if we need to lift throttles.

raj_eng: One more note: if they expect sustained throughput >50 rps during steady-state, recommend Dedicated/reserved capacity. For short ramps, CS can request a 10-minute quota increase in the support ticket. Also remind them to avoid per-request ephemeral tokens — that pattern almost always triggers onboarding guardrails.

customer-dev: Filing ticket now and will post id. Thanks all :thumbsup:
